title: Waste Declaration
next_chapter_hook: Han Lie sneered coldly: 'Wait and see how you self-destruct your cultivation'—he did not know that the chess game had already been laid out, while the prey remained utterly unaware.

text.content: Dawn had just broken, and the Blue Stone Plaza before the Tianqing Sect Mountain Gate was already bustling with voices. The Grand Tournament was three days away. Outer disciples, Inner disciples, and even some elders who had long remained unseen all made their appearances, the air thick with an atmosphere interweaving tension and anticipation. Chen Ji stepped through the Mountain Gate, the corners of his mouth slightly curving upward. He wore a faded gray robe, a copper token unique to Servant Disciples hanging at his waist, his steps neither hurried nor slow, as if he had come merely to watch an event that had nothing to do with him. Only in those deep eyes did a barely perceptible gleam flash.

The registration desk was set up beneath the corridor in front of the Martial Arena. A dozen tables stood in a neat row, with clerks each attending to their duties. The crowd wound like a long dragon, the noisy discussions rising and falling. 'I heard that even Han Lie, the first genius of Xuanwu Sect, will come to watch the competition this time!' 'Hmph, what business does an outsider have meddling here?' 'Don't you know? Han Lie declared he wants to see personally how the Tianqing Sect's 'Waste Senior Brother' makes a fool of himself on the Arena Platform.'

dialogue.content: 'Waste Senior Brother?' Chen Ji quietly repeated this designation, his tone betraying no emotionalfluctuation. He slightly tilted his head, glancing at the group of Outer disciples whispering at the corridor's end, a faint smile passing through his eyes. This title, he truly deserved. After all, in everyone's eyes, he truly was a genuine waste—a blocked meridian, poor spiritual energy circulation, ten years of cultivation yet still lingering at the third stage of Qi Refining.

text.content: Yet no one knew what kind of seven-aperture exquisite heart lay beneath this 'waste' skin. Chen Ji withdrew his gaze, slowly moving forward with the flow of people. He observed everything around him: which clerk was amicable, which one's eyes flickered with evasion, which area was crowded and prone to chaos... These details rapidly wove into a web in his mind, like a chess player surveying every piece on the board. Before long, he had reached the middle of the line.

dialogue.content: 'Make way! Make way!' A domineering voice came from behind the crowd. Everyone turned to look, only to see a sturdy young man striding forward like a comet, his entire being radiating a fierce aura. He wore the distinctive black combat attire of Xuanwu Sect, a jade pendant carved with the Xuanwu emblem at his waist, and his brows carried an air of proud arrogance. 'Han Lie! It's Han Lie from Xuanwu Sect!' 'Why is he here? Didn't he say he wouldn't arrive until the day of the competition?' The crowd parted automatically, everyone falling silent before him.

text.content: Han Lie walked to the front of the registration desk without regard for others, about to cut in line, when he suddenly caught sight of Chen Ji in the crowd. He paused, a playful arc curling at the corner of his mouth. 'Oh, isn't this the Tianqing Sect's Waste Senior Brother?' Han Lie turned to face Chen Ji, deliberately raising his voice, 'What, you're here to participate in the tournament too? With that demeanor of yours, is it because you haven't been humiliated enough?' Laughter erupted around him.

dialogue.content: Chen Ji raised his eyes, his gaze calmly meeting Han Lie's. He did not flare with anger, nor did his expression change in the slightest. He merely glanced at Han Lie indifferently, then retracted his gaze as if nothing had happened, continuing to look down at the copper token in his hand, as if this famous genius before him was merely an irrelevant gust of wind not worth acknowledging. Such disregard was more difficult to swallow than any counterattack.

text.content: Han Lie's face darkened. He was a once-in-a-century genius of Xuanwu Sect—when had anyone ever treated him with such contempt? 'Stop pretending to be mute! A waste is a waste, don't you even have the courage to retort?' Chen Ji finally raised his head again. He looked at Han Lie, a strange glint of amusement flickering in his eyes as he spoke: 'Young Master Han is right. I truly am a waste.'

At these words, the surroundings fell silent for a moment. The crowd exchanged bewildered glances, unable to understand what the Waste Senior Brother was up to. Some wore mocking smiles, others shook their heads and sighed, and some were already whispering amongst themselves: 'As expected, hopeless trash that cannot be propped up—even he acknowledges it himself.' Han Lie froze for an instant, then burst into laughter: 'At least you know your place! Wastes like you should老老实实stay in the Servants' Quarters scrubbing chamber pots. Why come out here to embarrass yourself?'

text.content: These words made Han Lie's expression shift slightly. Coming to Tianqing Sect to watch the tournament had always carried an air of bullying the weak; now that Chen Ji had pointed it out so bluntly, he suddenly felt he had been placed at a disadvantage. Laughter began to bubble up around them. 'The waste actually dares to talk back?'

dialogue.content: Chen Ji suddenly smiled, that smile carrying an indescribable, inexplicable meaning. 'Since Young Master Han thinks so highly of me, why don't we—' he spoke slowly, his voice soft yet clearly reaching everyone's ears, '—make a wager?'

text.content:
As soon as these words fell, the entire arena erupted in an uproar.

A waste who had only reached Qi Refining Third Layer actually wanted to make a bet with a genius at Foundation Building Peak? Had he gone mad from the stimulation, or was there something wrong with his brain?

Han Lie narrowed his eyes, studying Chen Ji as if looking at a jumping clown.

"What's the bet?"

Chen Ji walked calmly to the registration official, unhurriedly placing his copper token on the table. His movements were slow, as if deliberately creating some sense of ceremony.

"The bet is—" He lifted his head, his gaze calmly sweeping across the watching crowd before finally fixing on Han Lie's face, "—if I'm not a waste, I'll destroy my own cultivation on the spot."

These words were like a massive boulder thrown into a calm lake, stirring up a thousand waves.

"Did I hear that right? He wants to destroy his own cultivation?"
"Madness! This waste is absolutely mad!"
"Making such a vow in front of so many people—how will he back out?"

Even the registration official stood frozen, his vermillion brush suspended mid-air, not daring to make a mark. He glanced at Chen Ji, then at Han Lie, beads of fine sweat appearing on his forehead.

dialogue.content:
Han Lie froze for a full three breaths before bursting into wild laughter.

"Hahaha! Chen Ji, are you truly mad or just pretending?" He laughed so hard he doubled over, tears forming at the corners of his eyes, "Daring to say such things in front of all these people? Fine, young master will grant your wish!"

He turned to the registration official, his voice suddenly turning ice-cold: "Did you hear that? He himself said he would destroy his own cultivation. Bear witness!"

text.content:
The registration official's temples throbbed, caught in an impossible situation.

He knew Han Lie—the number one genius of Xuanwu Sect, with deep backing, not someone to offend. But no matter how much of a waste the person before him was, he was still a disciple of Tianqing Sect. Forcing someone to make such a vow publicly, if the sect investigated later, he wouldn't be able to escape responsibility either.

"Young Master Han, this... this probably isn't appropriate..." The official struggled to speak.

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji watched the official's distressed expression, a slight smile tugging at the corner of his mouth.

"Brother official," he said calmly, "I only said that if I'm not a waste, I would destroy my own cultivation. No one forced me. Besides—"

He paused, looking around at the surroundings, his voice neither too loud nor too soft, yet clear enough for everyone to hear:

"With so many senior brothers, senior sisters, junior brothers, and junior sisters present as witnesses. I, Chen Ji, have never denied being a waste."

text.content:
At these words, a commotion arose among the watching crowd.

Some began to回过神来, sensing something off in these words—Chen Ji had said 'if I'm not a waste' before destroying his cultivation, but he had never actually admitted to being a waste!

"Wait, his words..."
"Something seems off?"
"He never said he wasn't a waste, just 'if not'..."

Chen Ji seemed completely unaware of the crowd's reactions, still appearing leisurely and carefree.

"Since Young Master Han is so interested, why not add another stake?" he suggested with a smile, "If I truly am a waste, I'll destroy my cultivation; if I'm not..."

text.content: "If you're not, young master will kneel right here and kowtow three times, calling you master!" Han Lie agreed without suspicion, coldly adding. In his view, this bet had already placed him in an unbeatable position—how could a waste possibly not be a waste?

dialogue.content:
"Good, a promise is a promise." Chen Ji nodded, saying no more. He turned to the registration official: "Brother official, please register me. The tournament is in three days—I still need to go back and prepare well."

His tone was relaxed, as if that earth-shaking gamble had just been a casual joke.

text.content:
The registration official stared for a long while before reacting. He looked at Chen Ji's confident face, then at Han Lie's smug expression, feeling he had missed some crucial piece of information.

In the end, he still trembling, stamped the seal on Chen Ji's registration.

Han Lie watched Chen Ji take the registration document, unable to resist another sneer.

"Prepare? What can a waste prepare? Prepare how to lose gracefully on the Arena Platform?"

Chen Ji tucked the document into his chest, his movements composed. He didn't look at Han Lie, only slightly turning his head, his gaze falling on the distant Martial Arena—the tournament's venue.

"In three days, all will be revealed." he said calmly.

With that, he ignored Han Lie and walked straight toward the back of the registration line. He wanted to observe before leaving—who else was worth paying attention to.

The watching crowd parted automatically, their gazes toward Chen Ji becoming complicated.

Some called him a madman, some called him an idiot, and a few thought more deeply—did this waste Senior Brother seem different from the rumors?

Outside the crowd, a woman in blue robes stood quietly, taking in the entire scene.

Su Qingyao, Inner Disciple Senior Fellow of Tianqing Sect. She had only been passing by but was drawn to the spectacle. Now she slightly furrowed her brow, watching Chen Ji's departing figure, an inexplicable feeling rising in her heart.

"This waste..." she murmured to herself, "Those words just now—how could a waste possibly say something like that?"

dialogue.content: "Su Qingyao withdrew her gaze, about to leave when she heard the disciples beside her whispering: 'Han Lie is coming with full force this time, probably targeting Chen Ji.' 'Of course, last time at the sect exchange, Han Lie lost by a narrow margin and has been nursing a grudge. This time, under the pretense of watching the competition, he's here to settle scores. How could thattrash Chen Ji possibly be a match?' 'We'll have a good show in three days!' Su Qingyao's steps faltered, a cold glint flickering in her eyes.

text.content: "Meanwhile, on the other side of the crowd, an elderly man in gray robes was quietly observing everything. Ling Yuan, the former Sect Master of Tianqing Sect. Though hunched and frail, his clouded old eyes held a sharp, piercing light. 'Interesting.' he murmured to himself, his voice barely a whisper, 'Thistrash, he can actually keep his composure.' He turned and left, his withered figure quickly vanishing into the crowd, leaving behind a meaningful smile.

"The registration desk returned to its bustling chaos. Han Lie stood in place, his smug expression gradually fading, replaced by an inexplicable restlessness. Something felt off, but he couldn't pinpoint what. 'What tricks could atrash possibly pull?' he coldly snorted, 'In three days, young master will teach you what it means to regret!' With that, he stormed off, leaving behind a crowd of murmuring onlookers.

"Chen Ji walked out of the crowd, his pace neither fast nor slow. He looked up at the sky—the morning light had turned into bright daylight, spilling across the blue stone paths of Tianqing Sect, casting a faint golden glow. 'trash宣言...' he chuckled softly, 'That's actually a good name.' No one knew that beneath this surface of atrash Senior Brother, a complete chess game had already formed. On the arena platform three days later, he would show everyone what true 'playing pig to devour the tiger' really meant.

"Suddenly, a hoarse voice rang out in his mind: 'Boy, that move was well played.' It was Mo Xiansheng's voice—the remnant soul guardian, the guardian of the first page of the Tianji Record. Chen Ji's steps slightly faltered, his expression unchanged as he silently responded through divine sense: 'The elder flatters me. That was merely an appetizer; the main course is yet to come.' Mo Xiansheng's laughter echoed in the depths of his consciousness, carrying both satisfaction and anticipation.

"Chen Ji did not speak again, walking directly toward the Servants' Quarters. He strolled leisurely, as if truly just an idletrash, worrying about the upcoming competition. But if someone looked closely, they would notice his footsteps followed a peculiar rhythm, each step landing precisely on the junction of yin and yang. That was the Tianji Step recorded in the Tianji Record Fragment. On the surface, he was walking. In reality, he was perceiving everything around him through a unique frequency, constructing a three-dimensional map of the entire Tianqing Sect in his mind.

"Three days passed in the blink of an eye. On the day of the competition, the Martial Arena beneath Tianqing Sect's Peak was packed with people, banners fluttered, and horns blared. Chen Ji stood among the competing disciples, wearing a gray robe with faded cuffs slightly rolled up, revealing pale wrists. He kept his head down, looking timid—forming a stark contrast with the spirited fellow disciples around him. 'Thetrash Senior Brother actually came!' 'He's not here to die, is he?' 'I heard he made some bet with Han Lie? Truly courting death!'

"To these whispers, Chen Ji turned a deaf ear. His gaze swept past the crowd, landing on the imposing figures seated on the high platform—Sect Master Ling Yuan at the main seat, with peak leaders and elders on either side. In the Xuanwu Sect's observation area, Han Lie sat upright, a confident, assured smile on his face. In a corner of the crowd, Su Qingyao stood quietly, her gaze occasionally drifting toward Chen Ji's direction. The chessboard was set; only the first move remained.

dialogue.content: "Han Lie suddenly stood up, his gaze cutting through the crowd to lock onto Chen Ji. A cold smile curled at his lips as his voice, though not loud, clearly reached everyone present: 'Chen Ji—' Chen Ji raised his head, meeting his gaze. Han Lie spoke word by word: 'The three-day deadline has arrived. This young master wants to see exactly how you plan to self-destruct your cultivation!'

text.content: "At these words, the entire venue erupted in an uproar. 'Self-destruct cultivation? What self-destruct cultivation?' 'Didn't you hear? Three days ago during registration, Chen Ji publicly swore—saying if he wasn't atrash he'd self-destruct his cultivation!' 'Thistrash has gone mad! How dare he say such a thing?' 'Now Han Lie has brought it up publicly—how will he get out of this?' Countless eyes turned to Chen Ji in unison—some mocking, some curious, some worried, some gleeful.

"Chen Ji stood in place, facing Han Lie's provocation and the whole venue's议论, slowly raised his head, a faint smile appearing on his face. 'Han Gongzi, please don't be impatient.' His voice wasn't loud, yet it clearly spread across the entire venue: 'I said—if NOT atrash, then self-destruct cultivation. But who decided that I must prove I'm not atrash?'

"These words were like a basin of cold water, extinguishing the entire venue's commotion. Only then did everyone realize—Chen Ji had been playing word games from the start! He never admitted to being atrash, nor did he ever promise to prove he wasn't one. He only said 'if not atrash' then self-destruct cultivation—but what if he IS atrash? Then this vow needed no fulfillment at all! Han Lie's face turned livid; he almost spat blood. Thattrash had played him!

text.content:
No emotion could be seen on Ling Yuan's withered face. His turbid old eyes lingered on Chen Ji for a moment, and the corner of his mouth curved into a meaningful arc.

With his aged voice falling, drums and bells rang in unison across the Martial Arena Peak, officially commencing the tournament.

"Good... good one, Chen Ji!" He挤出这几个字 from between his teeth, voice full ofsuppressed的怒火, "On the arena platform, we'll meet!"

He knew that from this moment on, Han Lie had been thoroughly provoked. An opponent clouded by anger often makes more mistakes.

"We'll meet on the arena platform?" He轻笑 in his heart, "Young Master Han, are you certain you want to watch me废掉我的cultivation?"

The first round matchups were soon announced. When Chen Ji's name appeared in the首轮对手 column, laughter erupted around him.

trash?

He turned and left the crowd, heading toward the休息区.

Su Qingyao slightly frowned, her gaze lingering on his face for a moment, as if trying to discern something from those深邃的眼睛.

Chen Ji's footsteps didn't slow, only the corner of his mouth slightly lifting.

Having said this, he walked away without looking back.

Su Qingyao stood in place, watching his departing背影, a complex light flickering in her eyes. There was too much about thistrash that she couldn't see through.

Half an hour later, the tournament officially began.

Ten arenas at the foot of the Martial Arena Peak were simultaneously activated, with外门弟子的比试 taking place on the lowest three platforms. Elimination format—the first round was already elimination—one loss meant no more chances.

Chen Ji was assigned to the third arena, where opponent Zhang Meng had been waiting for quite some time. He held a pair of iron fists, muscles bulging all over, clearly a practitioner of external hard techniques.

Chen Ji calmly climbed onto the arena, steps light and floating, as if随时都会被风吹倒. He kept his head lowered, not daring to meet Zhang Meng's gaze, showing a perfect picture of cowardice and timidity.

Voices below the arena rose and fell.

The referee walked to the center of the arena, swept a glance over both contestants, and announced:

Chen Ji simply stood there quietly, eyes lowered, like a prisoner awaiting judgment.

Only he himself knew what kind of dangerous light was flickering in those垂下的眼眸深处.
